# CertificateAuthority

CertificateAuthority is a third-party certificate authority whose certificates Ziti accepts for enrollment and authentication. It is ready when it exists in Ziti as declared, verified or not: only the holder of its private key can verify it, see status.atProvider.verificationToken.

| | |
|---|---|
| API version | `ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1` |
| Scope | Namespaced |
| In Ziti | third-party certificate authority, `/edge/management/v1/cas` |
| Updated with | `PUT`: a setting that is left out of the spec is reset to the default of Ziti |

## Example

From [`examples/certificateauthority/certificateauthority.yaml`](../../examples/certificateauthority/certificateauthority.yaml):

```yaml
# A third-party certificate authority: identities such as the one in
# ../identity/ca.yaml enroll with certificates it issued.
#
# certPem is the certificate of your own certificate authority. The one below
# is a placeholder whose private key was thrown away, so nobody can verify it.
#
# The resource is ready as soon as the certificate authority exists in Ziti.
# Ziti accepts its certificates for authentication only once the certificate
# authority is verified, which takes its private key: sign a certificate with
# the common name in status.atProvider.verificationToken and post it to
# /edge/management/v1/cas/<id>/verify. status.atProvider.isVerified tells
# whether that happened.
apiVersion: ziti.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: CertificateAuthority
metadata:
  name: device-ca
spec:
  providerConfigRef:
    kind: ProviderConfig
    name: default
  forProvider:
    name: device-ca
    isAuthEnabled: true
    isOttCaEnrollmentEnabled: true
    isAutoCaEnrollmentEnabled: false
    certPem: |
      -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
      MIIBoDCCAUWgAwIBAgIUBC7NmEBB0amzuZXNt1MltavdjX8wCgYIKoZIzj0EAwIw
      HDEaMBgGA1UEAwwRRXhhbXBsZSBEZXZpY2UgQ0EwIBcNMjYxMDAyMjIzMjE2WhgP
      MjEyNjA5MDgyMjMyMTZaMBwxGjAYBgNVBAMMEUV4YW1wbGUgRGV2aWNlIENBMFkw
      EwYHKoZIzj0CAQYIKoZIzj0DAQcDQgAENm8FPnvuGAp1DZt1B8Hab5eKRB+iZF3F
      YN3wV/PRq2057rrZM9tMI0ZNTFHe8rC4fW+Yxaq0fWBRg9o66xb9haNjMGEwHQYD
      VR0OBBYEFFRjBSUc7WKDNHvIQ+34YgZWswZPMB8GA1UdIwQYMBaAFFRjBSUc7WKD
      NHvIQ+34YgZWswZPMA8GA1UdEwEB/wQFMAMBAf8wDgYDVR0PAQH/BAQDAgEGMAoG
      CCqGSM49BAMCA0kAMEYCIQCSmILSALCaVAjbxsN9zSlKLNqckbdKrhj0pExFj+Su
      qAIhALf/S4ORtC/m/+y6OGy/LknkoSlQTCnj4a4Qugq0x12v
      -----END CERTIFICATE-----
    tags:
      team: platform
```

## Settings: `spec.forProvider`

| Field | Type | Default | Field in Ziti | What it does in Ziti |
|-------|------|---------|---------------|----------------------|
| `name` | string, required |  | `name` | Name of the certificate authority. |
| `certPem` | string, required |  | `certPem` | CertPem is the PEM encoded certificate of the certificate authority. It must be a CA certificate that no other certificate authority in Ziti has, and it cannot be changed after creation. |
| `externalIdClaim` | object |  | `externalIdClaim` | ExternalIDClaim takes the external ID of an identity from its certificate. Without it, identities are recognized by the fingerprint of their certificate. Rule: the SCHEME matcher is for the SAN_URI location, which takes no PREFIX or SUFFIX matcher. Rule: matcherCriteria is required unless the matcher is ALL. Rule: parserCriteria is required for the SPLIT parser. |
| `externalIdClaim.index` | integer |  | `externalIdClaim.index` | Index of the external ID to use among the ones found, starting at zero. At least 0. |
| `externalIdClaim.location` | string | `COMMON_NAME` | `externalIdClaim.location` | Location of the values in the certificate: its common name, or the URIs or email addresses of its subject alternative names. One of `COMMON_NAME`, `SAN_URI`, `SAN_EMAIL`. |
| `externalIdClaim.matcher` | string | `ALL` | `externalIdClaim.matcher` | Matcher selects the values to consider: ALL of them, those with a PREFIX or a SUFFIX, or the URIs with a SCHEME. One of `ALL`, `PREFIX`, `SUFFIX`, `SCHEME`. |
| `externalIdClaim.matcherCriteria` | string |  | `externalIdClaim.matcherCriteria` | MatcherCriteria is the prefix, suffix or scheme the matcher looks for. |
| `externalIdClaim.parser` | string | `NONE` | `externalIdClaim.parser` | Parser turns a selected value into external IDs: NONE takes it as is, SPLIT splits it at a separator. One of `NONE`, `SPLIT`. |
| `externalIdClaim.parserCriteria` | string |  | `externalIdClaim.parserCriteria` | ParserCriteria is the separator of the SPLIT parser. |
| `identityNameFormat` | string | `[caName]-[commonName]` | `identityNameFormat` | IdentityNameFormat is the name of the identities that automatic enrollment creates. It may contain [caName], [caId], [commonName], [requestedName] and [identityId]. |
| `identityRoles` | list of strings |  | `identityRoles` | IdentityRoles are the role attributes of the identities that automatic enrollment creates. |
| `isAuthEnabled` | boolean |  | `isAuthEnabled` | IsAuthEnabled lets identities authenticate with a certificate of this certificate authority. |
| `isAutoCaEnrollmentEnabled` | boolean |  | `isAutoCaEnrollmentEnabled` | IsAutoCaEnrollmentEnabled lets anyone with a certificate of this certificate authority enroll, which creates an identity. |
| `isOttCaEnrollmentEnabled` | boolean |  | `isOttCaEnrollmentEnabled` | IsOttCaEnrollmentEnabled lets identities enroll with a one-time token and a certificate of this certificate authority. |
| `tags` | map of strings |  | `tags` | Tags is a map of tags. |

The settings every managed resource has, such as `spec.providerConfigRef`,
`spec.managementPolicies` and `spec.writeConnectionSecretToRef`, are described
in [Concepts](../concepts.md).

## Status: `status.atProvider`

| Field | Type | What it shows |
|-------|------|---------------|
| `name` | string | As Ziti reports it. |
| `createdAt` | string | As Ziti reports it. |
| `externalIdClaim` | object | ExternalIDClaim defines where in a client certificate the external ID of an identity is found. Rule: the SCHEME matcher is for the SAN_URI location, which takes no PREFIX or SUFFIX matcher. Rule: matcherCriteria is required unless the matcher is ALL. Rule: parserCriteria is required for the SPLIT parser. |
| `externalIdClaim.index` | integer | Index of the external ID to use among the ones found, starting at zero. At least 0. |
| `externalIdClaim.location` | string | Location of the values in the certificate: its common name, or the URIs or email addresses of its subject alternative names. One of `COMMON_NAME`, `SAN_URI`, `SAN_EMAIL`. |
| `externalIdClaim.matcher` | string | Matcher selects the values to consider: ALL of them, those with a PREFIX or a SUFFIX, or the URIs with a SCHEME. One of `ALL`, `PREFIX`, `SUFFIX`, `SCHEME`. |
| `externalIdClaim.matcherCriteria` | string | MatcherCriteria is the prefix, suffix or scheme the matcher looks for. |
| `externalIdClaim.parser` | string | Parser turns a selected value into external IDs: NONE takes it as is, SPLIT splits it at a separator. One of `NONE`, `SPLIT`. |
| `externalIdClaim.parserCriteria` | string | ParserCriteria is the separator of the SPLIT parser. |
| `fingerprint` | string | Fingerprint is the SHA-1 fingerprint of the certificate. |
| `id` | string | As Ziti reports it. |
| `identityNameFormat` | string | As Ziti reports it. |
| `identityRoles` | list of strings | As Ziti reports it. |
| `isAuthEnabled` | boolean | As Ziti reports it. |
| `isAutoCaEnrollmentEnabled` | boolean | As Ziti reports it. |
| `isOttCaEnrollmentEnabled` | boolean | As Ziti reports it. |
| `isVerified` | boolean | IsVerified is true once someone has proven to Ziti that they hold the private key of the certificate authority. Only then does Ziti accept its certificates for authentication and automatic enrollment. |
| `tags` | map of strings | As Ziti reports it. |
| `updatedAt` | string | As Ziti reports it. |
| `verificationToken` | string | VerificationToken is the common name of the certificate that proves it: a certificate with this common name, signed by the certificate authority, is posted to the verify endpoint of the Ziti API. |

## How it behaves

- The resource is ready when the certificate authority exists in Ziti as declared, verified or not. The provider cannot verify it: that takes a certificate signed with the private key of the certificate authority.
- `status.atProvider.verificationToken` is the common name the proof certificate must have. Sign a certificate with that common name with the key of the certificate authority and post it to `/edge/management/v1/cas/<id>/verify`. `status.atProvider.isVerified` tells whether it is done; until then Ziti does not accept certificates of the certificate authority.
- `certPem` cannot be changed after creation. `status.atProvider.fingerprint` tells which certificate Ziti holds.
- A certificate authority is replaced with `PUT`, because a `PATCH` drops its external ID claim. A setting that is left out of the spec is removed in Ziti or reset to its default.
- Deleting a certificate authority deletes the pending enrollments with its certificates. An [`IdentityCA`](identityca.md) that refers to it stays, but cannot enroll until the certificate authority exists again.
- A certificate authority that is deleted in Ziti is created anew and is not verified: it has to be verified again.

## When something goes wrong

- Ziti answers `400` about the certificate: `certPem` is not a CA certificate, or another certificate authority already has it.
- Identities cannot enroll or sign in with their certificates: the certificate authority is not verified, or `isAuthEnabled`, `isOttCaEnrollmentEnabled` or `isAutoCaEnrollmentEnabled` is off for what they try.

Create, update, drift, deletion in Ziti and deletion of the resource are covered by the end-to-end test, see [Testing](../testing.md).
